q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chapter II of Part XVII of the Constitution (Articles 345 to 347) is titled "Regional Languages".
2. Chapter IV of Part XVII of the Constitution (Special Directives) comprises Articles 350 and 351.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Part XVII Chapter II (Articles 345-347) is titled Regional Languages, and Chapter IV, Special Directives, comprises Articles 350 and 351, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the commencement of the Constitution, the number of languages included in the Eighth Schedule was 14.
2. After the inclusion of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in the Eighth Schedule in the year 1992, the total number of languages included in the Schedule became 18.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Eighth Schedule began with 14 languages, and the addition of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in 1992 raised the total from 15 to 18, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The standard of the Prabodh course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of the primary (Class V) level.
2. The standard of the Pragya course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Hindi standard of the matriculation (Class X) level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, Prabodh broadly matches Class V Hindi and Pragya broadly matches matriculation (Class X) Hindi, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India does not declare any language as the national language of India.
2. The expression used in Part XVII of the Constitution for the status of Hindi in the Union is "Official Language of the Union".
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: The Constitution declares no national language; Article 343 calls Hindi in Devanagari script the Official Language of the Union, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the National Education Policy, 2020, the three-language formula for school education will continue to be implemented, and no language will be imposed on any State.
2. Under the National Education Policy, 2020, wherever possible, the medium of instruction should be the mother tongue/local language until at least Class V.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: NEP 2020 continues the three-language formula with no language imposed on any State, and prefers mother tongue or local language as medium until at least Class V.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 344 of the Constitution, in making its recommendations, the Official Language Commission shall have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims and interests of persons belonging to the non-Hindi speaking areas in respect of public services.
2. Under Article 344(2) of the Constitution, the duty of the Official Language Commission includes making recommendations as to the form of numerals to be used for any one or more specified purposes of the Union.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 344 requires the Commission to regard non-Hindi speakers' claims in public services and advancement of India, and Article 344(2) covers the form of numerals.

q: A Rajbhasha note on railway institutions has to record the year in which the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was first constituted. The year to be recorded is:
e: The Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti, the advisory committee for Hindi in Railways, was first constituted in 1973.

q: A note on Rajbhasha committees in a Zonal Railway records the authority who chairs the Official Language Implementation Committee of the headquarters office of the Zonal Railway. The correct entry is:

options.A: The Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari
options.B: The Chief Personnel Officer
options.C: The General Manager
options.D: The Divisional Railway Manager

e: The Zonal Railway headquarters Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the General Manager, the head of the Zonal Railway.

q: An officer preparing a brief on linguistic minorities asks under which Ministry the office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions. The correct answer is:

options.A: The Ministry of Minority Affairs
options.B: The Ministry of Home Affairs
options.C: The Ministry of Education
options.D: The Ministry of Law and Justice

e: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, appointed under Article 350B, functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.

q: A note on the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities records the authority by whom those reports, relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities, are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to the Governments of the States concerned. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, that authority is:

options.A: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities himself
options.B: The Union Home Minister
options.C: The Prime Minister
options.D: The President

e: Under Article 350B, the President causes the Special Officer's reports on linguistic minority safeguards to be laid before Parliament and sent to State Governments.

q: In a Rajbhasha quiz, an employee is asked by which constitutional amendment Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution in the year 1992. The correct answer is:

options.A: The Constitution (21st Amendment) Act
options.B: The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act
options.C: The Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act
options.D: The Official Languages (Amendment) Act

e: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule in 1992 by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act.

q: A Rajbhasha quiz asks after whom the Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the official language, adopted by the Constituent Assembly in 1949, is named. The correct answer is:

options.A: K. M. Munshi and B. G. Kher
options.B: K. M. Munshi and G. B. Pant
options.C: K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
options.D: K. M. Munshi and Om Mehta

e: The 1949 Constituent Assembly formula is named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, its two principal movers.

q: An employee preparing a brief on the first Official Language Commission asks who chaired the Committee of Parliament which examined the recommendations of that Commission (the Kher Commission). The correct answer is:

options.A: G. B. Pant
options.B: Om Mehta
options.C: B. G. Kher
options.D: Lalit Narayan Mishra

e: The parliamentary committee that examined the first Official Language (Kher) Commission's recommendations was chaired by G. B. Pant.

q: For doing Hindi work on computers in a Central Government office, the dealing assistant is told to use a font/encoding so that the document can be read and exchanged on any computer system. The font/encoding to be used is:

options.A: A Unicode-compliant font (such as Mangal)
options.B: The Kruti Dev font, which is system-specific
options.C: Any ornamental English font with Hindi characters pasted as pictures
options.D: Hand-written text scanned and pasted into the document

e: Hindi work on computers must use a Unicode-compliant font such as Mangal, so documents can be read and exchanged on any system, unlike legacy fonts like Kruti Dev.

q: A newly posted station master asks in which languages announcements for the guidance of passengers are made at railway stations. The correct answer is:

options.A: Hindi only
options.B: English and the regional language only
options.C: Hindi and English only
options.D: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

e: Passenger announcements at railway stations are made in three languages: the regional language, Hindi and English, for the widest comprehension.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 1,000 letters during a quarter, of which 880 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 88 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 75 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'B'

e: 880 of 1,000 is 88 percent, below the Annual Programme target of 90 percent for Hindi-originating correspondence in Region B, so the office has fallen short.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 400 letters during a quarter, of which 240 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 75 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 60 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 240 of 400 is 60 percent, above the Annual Programme target of 55 percent for Hindi-originating correspondence in Region C, so the office has exceeded it.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' issued 1,000 letters during a quarter, all of which were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, no office being capable of reaching the prescribed target
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'A'

e: The Annual Programme target for Hindi-originating correspondence in Region A is 100 percent, so issuing all 1,000 letters in Hindi just meets the target.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 200 notes on files, of which 70 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 50 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target being 35 per cent
options.C: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi
options.D: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent

e: 70 of 200 notes is 35 percent, above the Annual Programme target of 30 percent for noting on files in Hindi, so the office has exceeded the target.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 120 notes on files, of which 30 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent
options.B: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 25 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target being 10 per cent
options.D: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi

e: 30 of 120 notes is 25 percent, below the Annual Programme target of 30 percent for noting on files in Hindi, so the office has fallen short.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 90 letters, of which 33 were originally written in Hindi and 57 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; translated English drafts do not, so the count is 33, not 90.

q: A senior accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 79 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, 79 percent marks fall in the band admissible for Rs 2,400.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 99 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 100 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.C: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks for the typewriting examination having been secured

e: A cash award for Hindi typewriting is admissible on securing 90 percent or more marks; 99 percent clears that threshold, so the award is admissible.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 82 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 12 months instead

e: A cash award for Hindi stenography requires 88 percent or more marks; 82 percent is below that threshold, so no cash award is admissible.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 29 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 25 words per minute
options.B: He does not pass on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination being 30 words per minute
options.C: He passes, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed passing speed for the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute; 29 words per minute therefore does not pass on speed.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 92 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 120 words per minute
options.C: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute
options.D: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting

e: The prescribed passing speed for the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute; 92 words per minute meets that standard.

q: A 35-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 30 years
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.C: He must undergo the training only after attaining the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee without working knowledge of Hindi who has not attained 45 years; at 35 he is not exempt.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 500, of whom 465 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 95 per cent or more
options.C: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 100 per cent
options.D: Notification is not permissible for offices located in Region 'C'

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 percent or more staff with working knowledge of Hindi; 465 of 500 is 93 percent, so the office can be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 9,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He becomes eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 5,000 words in a year
options.B: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration only if he repeats the performance in the following year
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is located in Region 'A'

e: Eligibility for the noting and drafting incentive requires at least 10,000 words in a year; 9,500 words falls short, so he is not eligible for consideration.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the seventh month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 6 months only
options.B: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again
options.C: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months
options.D: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible only from the thirteenth month onwards

e: Personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible for 12 months, so it continues in the seventh month.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 21,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 25,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.C: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices
options.D: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year

e: Eligibility for the noting and drafting incentive requires at least 10,000 words in a year; 21,000 words exceeds it, so he is eligible for consideration.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the eighteenth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months only
options.B: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for an indefinite period
options.C: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again
options.D: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 24 months

e: Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible for only 12 months, so its continuance in the eighteenth month is not in order.

q: A Central Government office spends 46 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for purchase of books. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, the prescribed target being 40 per cent
options.B: The claim is not in order, the prescribed target under the Annual Programme being at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for the library to be spent on Hindi books
options.C: The claim is in order only if the office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: No target is prescribed for purchase of books for office libraries

e: The Annual Programme requires at least 50 percent of library book purchase spending to be on Hindi books; 46 percent does not comply.

q: A Central Government office spends 54 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books. With reference to the Annual Programme target for purchase of books, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, the prescribed target being 75 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short, the prescribed target being 60 per cent
options.C: The office has complied with the target, the prescribed target being at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for the library to be spent on Hindi books
options.D: No target is prescribed for purchase of books for office libraries

e: Spending 54 percent on Hindi books exceeds the Annual Programme requirement of at least 50 percent of library purchase spending, so the target is complied with.

q: A town has fifteen Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town, the correct position is:

options.A: No Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted, the prescribed minimum being twenty Central Government offices
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted only with the approval of the Kendriya Hindi Samiti
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted only in metropolitan cities
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, such a committee being constituted in a town or city which has ten or more Central Government offices

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town or city having ten or more Central Government offices; fifteen offices qualify.

q: A town has six Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town, the correct position is:

options.A: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is not to be constituted, such a committee being constituted in a town or city which has ten or more Central Government offices
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the prescribed minimum being five Central Government offices
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted in every town, irrespective of the number of offices
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted only if all the offices are located in Region 'A'

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee requires ten or more Central Government offices in the town; six offices are below that minimum.

q: A Central Government office issues a press communique in English only, the dealing clerk contending that a press communique is a publicity document outside the language law. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, press communiques being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is not correct; a press communique is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 which must be issued in both Hindi and English
options.C: The contention is correct if the communique is issued in Region 'C'
options.D: The contention is correct if a Hindi version is supplied later on demand

e: Press communiques are listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, so they must be issued in both Hindi and English, not English only.

q: An administrative report of a Central Government office, which is to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, is prepared in Hindi only, the dealing assistant contending that preparation in the Official Language of the Union alone is sufficient. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, administrative reports being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is correct if the report is prepared in Region 'A'
options.C: The contention is not correct; such a report is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 which must be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: The contention is correct if an English summary is recorded on the file

e: Administrative reports to be laid before Parliament are listed in Section 3(3), so they must be issued in both Hindi and English, not Hindi only.

q: A Central Government office sends a circular written in Hindi to its field office located in Region 'C', without any translation. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: No accompaniment is required with the circular in any case
options.B: The circular must be accompanied by a translation in the regional language of that State
options.C: A covering letter in Hindi alone is sufficient accompaniment
options.D: The circular must be accompanied by its English translation

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a Hindi circular sent to Region C must be accompanied by its English translation.

q: A State Government office located in Region 'A' has to correspond with a Central Government office on an official matter. Ordinarily, such correspondence from the State Government office is conducted in:

options.A: Hindi
options.B: English only
options.C: The regional language, routed through the Governor's Secretariat
options.D: Both Hindi and English, every letter being issued in two copies

e: Correspondence from a State Government office in Region A to a Central Government office is ordinarily conducted in Hindi, the language of that region.

q: A Central Government office has to send a communication to a State which has adopted Hindi as its official language. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the language to be used for the communication is:

options.A: English only
options.B: Hindi
options.C: The regional language of that State
options.D: Hindi and English, in duplicate

e: Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, communications to a State that has adopted Hindi as its official language are to be in Hindi.

q: A note on Article 347 of the Constitution records the extent to which a language, directed by the President to be officially recognised on being satisfied that a substantial proportion of the population of a State desires its use to be recognised, may be so recognised. The correct entry is that such recognition may be:

options.A: For the whole of India
options.B: Only for use in the courts of that State
options.C: For the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as the President may specify
options.D: Only for a period of five years at a time

e: Under Article 347, Presidential recognition of a language may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as the President may specify.

q: An officer preparing a note on Article 350A of the Constitution has to record on whom the endeavour to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups rests. The correct entry is:

options.A: The Union Government alone
options.B: The State Government alone
options.C: The District Magistrate of the district
options.D: Every State and every local authority within the State

e: Article 350A places the endeavour to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage on every State and every local authority within the State.

q: A brief on Article 344 of the Constitution asks on which matters the Official Language Commission is to make recommendations to the President. The correct answer is:

options.A: The progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, restrictions on the use of English, the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts, and the form of numerals to be used
options.B: The translation of all Central Acts into Hindi
options.C: The inspection of Central Government offices for use of Hindi
options.D: The conduct of Hindi examinations for Government employees

e: Article 344 covers recommendations on progressive use of Hindi, restrictions on English, language of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and form of numerals.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Director". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Prabandhak
options.B: Nideshak
options.C: Sachiv
options.D: Adhyaksh

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Director is Nideshak, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Ministry". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Vibhag
options.B: Sachivalaya
options.C: Mantralaya
options.D: Nideshalaya

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Ministry is Mantralaya, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Ledger". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Khata Bahi
options.B: Panji
options.C: Roznamcha
options.D: Suchi Patra

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Ledger is Khata Bahi, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Noting". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Aadesh
options.B: Gyapan
options.C: Vivaran
options.D: Tippan

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Noting is Tippan, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Resignation". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Nilamban
options.B: Tyagpatra
options.C: Barkhastagi
options.D: Aavedan Patra

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Resignation is Tyagpatra, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Dearness Allowance". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Yatra Bhatta
options.B: Makan Kiraya Bhatta
options.C: Mahangai Bhatta
options.D: Pratipurti Bhatta

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Dearness Allowance is Mahangai Bhatta, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Vigilance". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Satarkta
options.B: Suraksha
options.C: Satyapan
options.D: Nirikshan

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Vigilance is Satarkta, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Priority". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Varishthata
options.B: Anukram
options.C: Kram
options.D: Prathmikta

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Priority is Prathmikta, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Arrears". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Shesh
options.B: Bakaya
options.C: Rin
options.D: Dhan Vapasi

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Arrears is Bakaya, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Affidavit". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Praman Patra
options.B: Yachika
options.C: Shapath Patra
options.D: Abhilekh

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Affidavit is Shapath Patra, as per official administrative terminology.

q: A dealing assistant preparing a Hindi noting has to write the standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Statistics". The correct equivalent is:

options.A: Sankalan
options.B: Ganit
options.C: Sarani
options.D: Sankhyiki

e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Statistics is Sankhyiki, as per official administrative terminology.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. The Central Hindi Directorate (Kendriya Hindi Nideshalaya) functions under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Central Translation Bureau is a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language, Home Affairs, while the Central Hindi Directorate is under Education.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.
2. The Official Language Resolution, embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, was adopted by Parliament in the year 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Hindi Diwas was first celebrated in 1953, marking 14 September 1949, and Parliament adopted the Official Language Resolution in 1968, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) was set up in the year 1967.
2. The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in the year 1985.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti was set up in 1967, and the Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in 1985, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) was set up in the year 1971.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was established in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Central Translation Bureau was set up in 1971, and the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra was established in 1960, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya) has its headquarters in Mauritius.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) is located at Agra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The World Hindi Secretariat is headquartered in Mauritius, and the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan is located at Agra, so both statements are correct.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' issued 800 letters during a quarter, of which 760 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 55 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'A'

e: 760 of 800 is 95 percent, below the 100 percent target for Hindi-originating correspondence in Region A, so the office has fallen short.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 250 letters during a quarter, of which 225 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 100 per cent
options.B: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 55 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent
options.D: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 95 per cent

e: 225 of 250 is 90 percent, exactly the Annual Programme target for Hindi-originating correspondence in Region B, so the office has just met it.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 1,000 letters during a quarter, of which 500 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.B: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 50 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 40 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 500 of 1,000 is 50 percent, below the 55 percent target for Hindi-originating correspondence in Region C, so the office has fallen short.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 250 notes on files, of which 100 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 50 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 40 per cent
options.C: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi
options.D: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent

e: 100 of 250 notes is 40 percent, above the 30 percent target for noting on files in Hindi, so the office has exceeded the target.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 160 notes on files, of which 40 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 20 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 25 per cent
options.D: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi

e: 40 of 160 notes is 25 percent, below the 30 percent target for noting on files in Hindi, so the office has fallen short.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 140 letters, of which 56 were originally written in Hindi and 84 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; translated English drafts do not, so the count is 56, not 140.

q: An accounts clerk passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 66 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.B: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 70 per cent

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, 66 percent marks fall in the band admissible for Rs 1,600.

q: A senior accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 78 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, 78 percent marks fall in the band admissible for Rs 2,400.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 93 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 95 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks for the typewriting examination having been secured
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 12 months instead

e: A cash award for Hindi typewriting requires 90 percent or more marks; 93 percent clears that threshold, so the award is admissible.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 89 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent marks
options.C: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks
options.D: A cash award is admissible only if his typewriting speed exceeds 40 words per minute

e: A cash award for Hindi typewriting requires 90 percent or more marks; 89 percent is below it, so no cash award is admissible.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 91 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks for the stenography examination having been secured
options.B: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi typewriting examination
options.D: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award

e: A cash award for Hindi stenography requires 88 percent or more marks; 91 percent clears that threshold, so the award is admissible.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 87 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent marks
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 12 months instead
options.D: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks

e: A cash award for Hindi stenography requires 88 percent or more marks; 87 percent is below it, so no cash award is admissible.

q: A Central Government office located at Nagpur in the State of Maharashtra issued 600 letters during a quarter, of which 480 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for Maharashtra being 75 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B', in which Maharashtra is placed, being 90 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 55 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices located in Maharashtra

e: Nagpur in Maharashtra is in Region B, where the target is 90 percent; 480 of 600 is 80 percent, so the office has fallen short.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 86 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.C: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute
options.D: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting

e: The prescribed passing speed for Hindi stenography is 80 words per minute; 86 words per minute meets that standard.

q: A 39-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.B: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 35 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training only after attaining the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee without working knowledge of Hindi who has not attained 45 years; at 39 he must undergo it.

q: An employee aged 49 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is proposed to be nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for him irrespective of his age
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.C: He must undergo the training only if he is posted in Region 'C'
options.D: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for him, he having attained the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory after attaining 45 years, so for an employee aged 49 it is not compulsory.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 150, of whom 135 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 95 per cent or more
options.B: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office cannot be notified, notification depending only on the total number of staff
options.D: The office can be notified only with the approval of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 percent or more staff with working knowledge; 135 of 150 is 90 percent, so the office can be notified.

q: A Central Government office has a total staff strength of 180, of whom 126 have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 60 per cent or more
options.B: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 70 per cent or more
options.C: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: Notification is not permissible for offices located in Region 'B'

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 percent or more staff with working knowledge; 126 of 180 is 70 percent, so the office cannot be notified.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 200 letters, of which 90 were originally written in Hindi and 110 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; translated English drafts do not, so the count is 90, not 200.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 6,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He becomes eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 5,000 words in a year
options.B: He becomes eligible for consideration only if he repeats the performance in the following year
options.C: He is eligible only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year

e: Eligibility for the noting and drafting incentive requires at least 10,000 words in a year; 6,500 words falls short, so he is not eligible.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the fifth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 3 months only
options.B: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months
options.C: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again
options.D: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible only from the thirteenth month onwards

e: Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible for 12 months, so its continuance in the fifth month is in order.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 17,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices

e: Eligibility for the noting and drafting incentive requires at least 10,000 words in a year; 17,500 words exceeds it, so he is eligible.

q: A Central Government office spends 62 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books. With reference to the Annual Programme target for purchase of books, the position is:

options.A: The office has complied with the target, at least one-half of the amount spent on purchase of books for the library being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed proportion being 75 per cent
options.C: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed proportion being 90 per cent
options.D: No target is prescribed for purchase of books for the library

e: Spending 62 percent on Hindi books complies, as at least one-half of library book purchase spending must be spent on Hindi books.

q: A Central Government office spends 38 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for purchase of books. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, the prescribed proportion being 25 per cent
options.B: The claim is in order, no target being prescribed for purchase of books
options.C: The claim is in order, the prescribed proportion being one-third of the amount
options.D: The claim is not in order, at least one-half of the amount spent on purchase of books for the library being required to be spent on Hindi books

e: Spending only 38 percent on Hindi books does not comply, as at least one-half of library purchase spending must be spent on Hindi books.

q: A town has twelve Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town, the correct position is:

options.A: No Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted, the prescribed minimum being twenty Central Government offices
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, such a committee being constituted in a town which has ten or more Central Government offices
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted only in a State capital
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted only during Hindi Pakhwada

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town having ten or more Central Government offices; twelve offices qualify.

q: A town has eight Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town, the correct position is:

options.A: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, such a committee being constituted in every town
options.B: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the prescribed minimum being five Central Government offices
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is not to be constituted, such a committee being constituted in a town which has ten or more Central Government offices
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted only with the approval of the President

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee requires ten or more Central Government offices; eight offices are below that minimum.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Rules, 1976 have been framed by the Central Government in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
2. The Committee of Parliament on Official Language was constituted in the year 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Official Language Rules, 1976 were framed under Section 8 of the Act, and the Committee of Parliament on Official Language was constituted in 1976.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Official Language Commission was appointed in the year 1955 under the chairmanship of B. G. Kher.
2. Under Article 344 of the Constitution, the President shall constitute an Official Language Commission at the expiration of five years from the commencement of the Constitution, and thereafter at the expiration of ten years from such commencement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The first Official Language Commission was appointed in 1955 under B. G. Kher, as Article 344 requires a Commission after five years and again after ten years.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, every person is entitled to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be.
2. Article 350A of the Constitution relates to facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 350 allows a grievance representation in any language used in the Union or the State, and Article 350A covers mother-tongue instruction for linguistic minorities.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language.
2. The Official Language Implementation Committee constituted in a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: The Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language, and an office committee by the head of office.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Official Language was set up as a separate department in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the year 1975.
2. The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology functions under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Department of Official Language was set up separately in the Ministry of Home Affairs in 1975, and the Terminology Commission functions under Education.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Pakhwada is observed in Central Government offices and Railways from 14th September to 28th September every year.
2. Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Hindi Pakhwada is observed from 14 to 28 September every year, and Hindi Diwas was first celebrated in 1953, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1975 at Nagpur.
2. The Third World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1983 at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The first World Hindi Conference was held in 1975 at Nagpur, and the third was held in 1983 at New Delhi, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sindhi language was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967.
2. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Sindhi entered the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Amendment, 1967, and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd Amendment, 2003, so both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Gazette of India is published in both Hindi and English.
2. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Gazette of India is published in Hindi and English, and the Rules require Central Government office letter-heads to be printed in Hindi and English.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi workshops organised in Central Government offices give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi.
2. The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is required to be sent by a Central Government office every quarter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Hindi workshops give practical training for noting and drafting in Hindi, and the Quarterly Progress Report on Hindi use is sent every quarter, so both are correct.

q: A Hindi translation of a Central Act, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, is placed before an officer, who contends that it is only a summary prepared for the guidance of officers. The correct position under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is:

options.A: The contention is not correct; the translation is deemed to be the authoritative text of the Act in Hindi
options.B: The contention is correct; a Hindi translation has no legal status
options.C: The contention is correct if the translation is used only in Region 'A' States
options.D: The contention is not correct only after the translation is approved by the State Legislature

e: Under Section 5, a Hindi translation of a Central Act published under the President's authority in the Gazette is deemed the authoritative text in Hindi.

q: To ensure that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, a Central Government office designates certain points in the office, such as the despatch section, through which such documents pass before issue. Such designated points are known as:

options.A: Hindi cells
options.B: Translation points
options.C: Check points
options.D: Issue counters

e: Points designated to ensure Section 3(3) documents issue bilingually, such as the despatch section, are known as check points.

q: In the year 1960, a member of Parliament seeks to introduce a Bill relating to the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts, without the previous sanction of the President. Under Article 349 of the Constitution, the correct position is:

options.A: The Bill may be introduced, no sanction being required for a language Bill
options.B: The Bill cannot be introduced, the previous sanction of the President being required for such a Bill during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution
options.C: The Bill may be introduced with the approval of the Prime Minister alone
options.D: The Bill may be introduced with the consent of the Chief Justice of India alone

e: Article 349 required the President's previous sanction, during the first fifteen years, for a Bill on language for the Supreme Court and High Courts; 1960 was within it.

q: An author writes an original book in Hindi on a subject specified for the purpose and submits it for an award of the Department of Official Language given for original book writing in Hindi. The award for which his book is to be considered is:

options.A: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar
options.B: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield
options.C: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield
options.D: The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar

e: The Department of Official Language award for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects is the Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar.
